cards.text: This is a psalm of David, written for the choirmaster, and he's talking straight to the LORD. He opens with, "O LORD, You have searched me and known me." Friend, I got searched every single time somebody dug through my junk drawer looking for tape, but NOBODY ever knew me.

cards.question: David says the LORD knows when he sits down and when he gets up. What else does the LORD understand from afar?

cards.text: And David keeps going. The LORD searches out his path and his lying down, and He's aware of ALL his ways: the couch, the hallway, the 2 a.m. tiptoe to the cookie jar, ALL of it.

cards.question: David says the LORD only knows his words after he says them out loud.

cards.text: Then David says the LORD hems him in behind and before, and has laid His hand on him. Behind AND before, friend, so there's no side door on this one.

cards.question: The LORD knows David inside and out. How does David describe that kind of knowledge?

answers.text: Too wonderful for him to reach
Simple enough for him to explain
Heavy enough to wear him out

cards.text: Then David asks two questions: "Where can I go to escape Your Spirit? Where can I flee from Your presence?" Buckle up, friend, because he's about to picture every hiding spot there is.

cards.question: If David went up to the heavens, or made his bed in Sheol, what does he say he'd find in both places?

cards.text: Next he pictures rising on the wings of the dawn, or settling by the farthest sea. That's the "new phone number, no forwarding address" plan, and somebody ALWAYS still finds you.

cards.question: Even by the farthest sea, David says the LORD's hand will ___ him.

cards.text: Last idea: what if David says the darkness will surely hide him, and the light around him will become night? Friend, I spent YEARS in the dark at the back of a junk drawer, so trust me, I know a good hiding spot when I see one.

cards.question: Why can't the darkness hide David from God?

answers.text: Darkness is as light to God

cards.question: The heavens, Sheol, the farthest sea, the dark. What's David's point in naming all these places?

answers.text: There's nowhere God isn't with him
Some places are too far for God
God only follows when he calls

cards.text: Now David goes back before he was even born: the LORD formed his inmost being and knit him together in his mother's womb. KNIT him, friend, and I still need three tries to tie my own apron.

cards.question: Thinking about how God made him, what does David do?

cards.text: David says he was made in secret, woven together in the depths of the earth. Out of sight. WAY out of sight.

cards.question: Even though he was made in secret, David says his frame was not ___ from God.

cards.text: And God's eyes saw David's body while it was still unformed. That's seeing the cookie before the dough's even mixed.

cards.question: David says all his days were written in God's book only after he lived them.

cards.text: This floors David. He says, "How precious to me are Your thoughts, O God, how vast is their sum!"

cards.question: If David tried to count God's thoughts, what does he say they would outnumber?

cards.text: Then David says, "when I awake, I am still with You." Count till you doze off, friend, and you still wake up right where you started.
Then the psalm takes a hard turn. David says, "O God, that You would slay the wicked," and he tells the bloodthirsty men to get away from him.

cards.question: David wants the bloodthirsty men away from him. What does he say they do?

cards.text: David asks, "Do I not hate those who hate You, O LORD, and detest those who rise against You?"

cards.question: David says he counts the people who rise against the LORD as his friends.

cards.text: Then David asks for the very thing he opened with: "Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me and know my concerns." Remember all those hiding spots, friend? Now David's pulling the drawer wide open HIMSELF.

cards.question: As God searches him, what does David ask God to see?

answers.text: If there's any offensive way in him
That he's better than the wicked

cards.question: David's last request is to be led somewhere. Where?

findings.problem: David appears for the first time as just 'a psalm of David'. The card never says simply who he is, like 'David, king of Israel'.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The joke puts modern details (the couch, the hallway, a 2 a.m. trip to the cookie jar) straight into David's ways, as if they were part of what the text describes. The comparison is blended with the Bible setting instead of standing as its own image.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: 'Behind AND before, so there's no side door' doesn't follow. Behind and before says nothing about the sides, so the punchline undercuts its own logic and leaves a reader puzzled.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The right answer 'Darkness is as light to God' is a near-quote of the verse and sounds like the Bible. The wrong answers ('God waits for the morning', 'David's voice gives him away') are plain modern phrasing, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 5 of 7 choice cards are multiple choice, with only 1 true or false and 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Verse 14's central line, 'I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Marvelous are Your works', is never told or asked. The card only asks that David praises God, so the baker misses the key detail of the verse.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences ('David says... earth.' / 'Out of sight.' / 'WAY out of sight.').

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'This floors David' states David's emotional reaction as fact. It also ties verse 17 to verse 16 as cause and effect, which the text doesn't say. It should be marked as Papa Dorin's guess.

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The punchline 'you still wake up right where you started' reads as no progress or a reset count. That muddies the verse's point that David wakes still with God, and the line doesn't click without explaining.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: Card 12 just quoted David saying he detests those who rise against the LORD, so asking whether he counts them as friends is given away by the setup. The verse's own striking detail, 'perfect hatred', is also never told.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: the quote sentence, 'Remember all those hiding spots, friend?' and 'Now David's pulling the drawer wide open HIMSELF.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'David's pulling the drawer wide open HIMSELF' puts Papa Dorin's junk drawer into David's prayer. The comparison is blended into the Bible setting.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Far from the wicked' is arguable. In verse 19 David says 'away from me, you bloodthirsty men', so a baker could argue he wants distance from the wicked. Also, 'In the way everlasting' sounds more like the Bible than the other two answers.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 5 of 8 choice cards are multiple choice, with 2 true or false and only 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
